questions.question: The term -dx/dt in the rate expression refers to the:
options: increase in the concentration of reactants.
questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of reaction ±dxdt represents the rate of change of the concentration of a reactant or product with respect to time at a specific moment in time. It gives the rate of reaction at an exact point in time, which can be determined by taking the derivative of the concentration of a species with respect to time. This instantaneous rate of reaction can vary throughout the course of the reaction, depending on factors such as the concentrations of reactants and products, temperature, and presence of catalysts.

questions.question: Order of reaction can be:
questions.explanation: The order of a reaction is not necessarily an integer. Fractional: Fractional orders, both positive and negative, represent more intricate relationships between concentrations and rate in more complex reactions.
